lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: understand how organisms are able to respond to changes in their environment

primer.text: You already know that living things share characteristics such as sensitivity and movement. This note gives the sensitivity characteristic its exam vocabulary: what a stimulus is, which cells detect it, and the kinds of response organisms make. It is the doorway note for every control system that follows in this subtopic.

modules.title: Detecting change and answering it
modules.opening: Survival depends on noticing change. Every organism detects stimuli — shifts in light, temperature, sound, chemicals or touch — through receptor cells, then produces a response that improves its odds. Humans house receptors in sense organs, plants use specialised cells for light, gravity or water, and both answer change with movement, secretion or adjusted processes.
keyPoints: Organisms detect and respond to change in order to survive.
A stimulus is any detectable change in surroundings — light, temperature, sound, chemicals or touch.
Receptors do the detecting: in sense organs for humans, specialised cells for plants.
Responses include moving toward or away, secreting chemicals, or adjusting body processes.
A useful response raises the organism's chance of survival.

low.restatement: Detect the change, then answer it — movement, secretion or internal adjustment that aids survival.
low.analogy: A sunflower swivelling to face the sun is detecting light and responding by reorienting its head.
low.examPointer: Give a named stimulus-and-response pair whenever a question asks how organisms respond to their environment.

medium.restatement: Detection and response form a survival loop: receptor cells convert external or internal change into action, keeping feeding, escape and internal balance on track.
medium.analogy: It is a smoke-alarm routine: sense the smoke, sound the alert, evacuate — each step protects the household.
medium.examPointer: Tie the response back to survival explicitly — escaping predators, finding food and maintaining internal conditions are the examiner's examples.

glossary.definition: A detectable change in the internal or external environment, such as light, temperature or sound.
A cell that detects a stimulus; found in sense organs in humans and as specialised cells in plants.
The action an organism produces after detecting a stimulus, such as moving, secreting or adjusting body processes.
